=== FINDINGS ===

F1 MAJOR — ORC-CTRL-1's '28 of 37 armed' count still counts the C1–C14 flips column as arms, and those controls do not exist on disk. (spec.md:763-767 says 'The 15 in the flips column below (ARB-1, ARB-2, ARB-3, DASH-2, DASH-3, DASH-5, PAUSE-1, PAUSE-2, POL-2, POL-7, PROV-1, REG-1, REG-2, REG-3, REG-4)' are part of the 28 armed.) The C1–C14 table (spec.md:630-646) is the *planned* mandatory core: ORC-CTRL-2 (spec.md:805) says 'Controls are written before implementation (P3 precedes P4)' and §0 (spec.md:50) says 'the test phase writes one seeded arm (flip) and one null arm (green) for every normative id'. No arm implementing any C1–C14 control exists on disk: grepping the whole tests/ + tools/ tree for each C-control's seeded-defect marker ('quiet store + clean policy file', 'an entry with no owner/reason refused', 'env knob with no file entry', '6-hour-old unconditional pause', 'pause --until-done T<x>', 'a section rendering a number not in store/policy', 'one-edit onboarding', 'shed queue-first') returns nothing; and each of the 15 flips ids (ARB-1, ARB-2, ARB-3, DASH-2, DASH-3, DASH-5, PAUSE-1, PAUSE-2, POL-2, POL-7, PROV-1, REG-1, REG-2, REG-3, REG-4) is named in NO test file on disk. So 15 of the claimed 22/28 'armed' ids are armed by a plan, not by an arm — the exact overclaim T778 finding 1 flagged in rev 1 ('16 wishes wearing requirements'), restated with a count instead of a universal claim. What is on disk: 7 ids genuinely armed by T802 (POL-1, POL-3, POL-4, GATE-2, DASH-1, DASH-4, ARB-4 — RED arms verified present and run: 31 tests, 9 expected failures, OK) and 5 of T813's 6 (POL-8..12); POL-13 (see F2). So the honest armed count at HEAD is 12 of 37, not 28 of 37, and the '9 unarmed enumerated' list (GOAL-1..4, POL-5, POL-6, PAUSE-3, GATE-1, ORIENT-1) is wrong in composition — 25 ids are unarmed on disk. What would refute: a file implementing C1–C14 (a C-battery), or any test naming one of the 15 flips ids.

F2 MAJOR — POL-13 is claimed armed by T813 but has no arm, and §14's own 'no id is added unarmed' is false. (spec.md:767-769 lists POL-13 among '6 armed by T813'; §14 rev3 closing line says 'The 6 new ids (POL-8…13) each carry an arm; … no id is added unarmed.') POL-13 (spec.md:412) is 'a cooldown is legible or it does not exist. Every cooldown renders on the dashboard as one row — what (scope), why (reason), when (end) — beside the pauses section (ORC-PAUSE-3, ORC-DASH-4).' The T813 arms named in §14 row 4 — test_todays_auto_cooldown_is_one_narrow_case and test_cooldown_carries_reason_end_and_scope — assert scope/reason/end existence in window_policy.py text (POL-11/12's subject); NEITHER asserts dashboard rendering/legibility, and 'POL-13' appears in the test file only in a comment header (tests/unit/test_s06_conformance.py:347), never as an assertion. grep for 'POL-13' in the test file: 0 assertion hits; grep for 'renders on the dashboard' / 'legible' across tests/: 0. So an id is claimed armed whose arm does not test what the id says — MAJOR per the audit brief's own rule. What would refute: a test asserting POL-13's dashboard-row content.

F3 MAJOR — ORC-GOAL-2's '3479 lines at the spec's own pin' and the per-file column '@a1415fe' are wrong at the pin: watch-fleet.sh is 286 lines at a1415fe, not 304. (spec.md:90 says 'untracked/watch-fleet.sh | 304 | 311'; spec.md:92 says 'Six files, 3479 lines at the spec's own pin'.) Verified: git show a1415fe:untracked/watch-fleet.sh | wc -l = 286 (three counting methods agree); 304 is the count at 402922f (T739, 13:10:21, six minutes AFTER the pin a1415fe at 13:04:59). The corrected sum is 1169+737+176+536+557+286 = 3461, not 3479. The 8c00704 column checks out (1169+548+176+546+858+311 = 3608). So the load-bearing delta (3608-3479=129 'grew by 129 lines in eight hours') is actually 147 lines — the argument survives directionally, but the number the argument rests on is wrong at the spec's own pin, and the spec's own citation-pin rule (spec.md:20-22: 'A citation that no longer resolves at a1415fe is a spec defect') makes this a spec defect. What would refute: showing watch-fleet.sh at 304 at a1415fe.

F4 MAJOR — the operator's interleave ruling is absent from the spec, and pass 1 as written can leave the fleet undispatchable mid-flight. Roadmap §7 (docs/status/roadmap-2026-08-23.md:308-316) records the binding ruling: 'after each pass lands, the fleet dispatches ordinary unrelated work through the changed mechanism before the next pass begins. A pass is not complete when its own arms are green; it is complete when unrelated tasks have gone through the changed door and closed cleanly.' The spec never mentions interleave/unrelated work: grep for 'interleave|unrelated|ordinary work|smoke work' in spec.md and STATUS.md returns nothing (spec's only 'smoke' is ORC-PLAN-3's per-commit 'commit → deploy → smoke', spec.md:658 — that is tools/smoke.sh, not the interleave rule). STATUS.md's pass protocol ('Per pass: commit → deploy → smoke → the pass's own arms green → then the next') likewise omits it. Separately, pass 1 'absorbs window_policy.py, directive_policy.py, the cooldown half of fleet-keeper.sh' (spec.md:660) with ABSORB defined as 'coverage re-expressed as managent Zig tests, shell script retired at phase close' (spec.md:674) — but bin/dispatch (imports at lines 86-87 at HEAD / 87-88 at 8c00704), bin/subagent (line 70) and tools/runner (line 128) import those modules TODAY, and dispatch/subagent rewire happens at step 5 (spec.md:664-665). Nothing in the spec states the absorbed modules survive until step 5, or that step 1 rewires the import sites; a literal reading of pass 1 (retire the two policy modules at phase close) breaks every dispatch until step 5, directly contradicting the interleave ruling's requirement that the fleet dispatch ordinary work between passes. What would refute: a spec sentence stating the old modules' survival window or an interleave step in ORC-PLAN-3.

F5 MEDIUM — ORC-POL-4's '(§6 specifies the states.)' is a wrong cross-reference: §6 is the Registration flow, not the cooldown state machine. (spec.md:202 says 'each cooldown's arithmetic survives as a named state of the machine. (§6 specifies the states.)' — but §6, spec.md:557, is 'Registration flow (ruling 5) — file-first, one writer, required fields'.) The cooldown states are named in ORC-GATE-2 (spec.md:604-606: heal · dispatch · window · global-keeper-flag) and §12 explicitly defers 'the merged cooldown machine's exact state set and transitions (ORC-GATE-2)' to design (spec.md:913). A builder following the ORC-POL-4 parenthetical lands in the registration section and finds no states; the parenthetical is stale (likely from a rev-1 numbering where §6 was the arbiter section). What would refute: §6 containing a state-machine specification.

The imports themselves are live at all three (the substantive census claim is correct); the line numbers are wrong under the spec's own pin convention. What would refute: the imports at the cited lines at a1415fe.

F8 MINOR — §14's preamble count is stale after T813: spec.md:942-943 still says '24 arms — 19 GREEN characterization, 5 RED spec-conformance covering 7 ids' while the body's ORC-CTRL-1 claims 28 of 37 armed and the test file itself now declares 31 arms / 22 GREEN / 9 RED covering 13 ids (tests/unit/test_s06_conformance.py:23-27). The §14 header was not updated when T813 added 7 arms, so the same document states two different arm totals (24 in §14's preamble, 31 in the file it names). === WHAT PASSES (verified, not findings) ===
The census's substance is correct: window_policy.py IS imported at both front doors (bin/dispatch + bin/subagent), directive_policy.py at bin/dispatch + tools/runner; the two modules were on a no-production-caller list and are in fact gating every dispatch. The keeper incident is live and real: pid 99956 alive (verified ps), last dispatch 2026-08-20T18:25:26Z T554 → claude-fable-5 (verified in untracked/log/fleet-keeper.log line 3514), 8,985 'cooldown flag set — no new dispatches' ticks in the log (grown from the 8,747 the census counted; still growing), the bare flag file exists (0 bytes, 2026-08-20 20:28), and no launchd job is loaded (verified launchctl list). The regression-script counts are right at their pins: 75 at a1415fe, 80 at 8c00704, 81 at HEAD (all three verified with git ls-tree / ls), and the disposition arithmetic 19+16+45+0=80 plus T801's 1 = 81 holds; TestDispositionCount runs green. The appetite-table disagreement (finding 11) is real: fleet-keeper.sh:325 says ollama=SPEND, main.zig:313 (at 8c00704) says ollama-cloud=OFF; family names differ; the 0-9 dial exists in no source file. The DASH-4/PLAN-3 empty-intersection claim is real: watch-fleet renders PROGRESS/CONCERNS/RECENT/DONE/OPEN, none of the five specified sections. T802's four findings (rows 9-12) are each re-verified against disk. The 7 T802 RED arms and 5 T813 RED/GREEN arms exist and run (31 tests, 9 expected failures, OK, 0.04s).

=== MILESTONE ===
Advances L1 (hands-off orchestration) — but cuts AGAINST it: the armed-count claim that was the rev-2 ratification basis is still overstated by 16 at rev 3 (C1-C14 battery is a plan, not arms), POL-13 is claimed armed with no arm, and the spec still does not carry the operator's interleave ruling — so the sprint cannot be built as written, and the fleet would break between pass 1 and pass 5 under a literal reading.
